entries.why_context_sensitive: Explicit @ forces implicit intersection of the column range A1:A3 against the caller's row. The result depends on the caller location relative to the range, which only exists in a bound worksheet context.
entries.expected_behavior: With the caller on row 1, implicit intersection of A1:A3 picks the value on the caller's row: 10.

entries.why_context_sensitive: Explicit @ over a row range intersects against the caller's column. The picked element depends on caller column, a bound-context fact.
entries.expected_behavior: With the caller in column E (outside A:C on the same row), Excel returns #VALUE! because the implicit intersection has no overlapping column. Caller column within A:C returns that column's value.

entries.why_context_sensitive: SEQUENCE(3) yields a dynamic-array column; explicit @ collapses it by implicit intersection against the caller row. Requires dynamic-array evaluation plus caller-relative intersection.
entries.expected_behavior: With the caller on row 1, @ on the 3-tall array {1;2;3} returns the caller-row element: 1.

entries.why_context_sensitive: OFFSET returns a reference (a 3x1 range A2:A4); explicit @ then implicitly intersects it against the caller. Both the reference transform and the intersection are context-bound.
entries.expected_behavior: OFFSET(A1,1,0,3,1) is A2:A4; @ against caller row 1 has no overlap, so Excel returns #VALUE!. A caller row within rows 2-4 returns that row's value.

entries.why_context_sensitive: OFFSET produces a derived reference from a base cell and offsets; SUM then enumerates the derived range. The reference transform requires a resolver that can offset a real reference, which OxFunc does not own in isolation.

INDEX with row_num 0 returns the entire column 2 as a reference (B1:B3), not a scalar. SUM then enumerates that derived reference. The reference-returning form of INDEX is a reference transform the OxFunc provider does not resolve without binding.
entries.expected_behavior: INDEX(A1:C3,0,2) is the reference B1:B3; SUM = 2+5+8 = 15.

entries.why_context_sensitive: INDIRECT builds a reference from runtime text and resolves it against the workbook. Resolving the assembled A1-style string to a live cell requires host reference resolution.
entries.expected_behavior: B1 is 2, so the text is "A2"; INDIRECT("A2") dereferences A2 = 22.

entries.why_context_sensitive: CELL reports host-level metadata (address, format, sheet) about a reference. The answer is a property of the workbook/host, not of any value OxFunc can compute alone.
entries.expected_behavior: CELL("address",A1) returns the absolute address text "$A$1".

entries.why_context_sensitive: FORMULATEXT returns the literal formula string of the referenced cell, which only exists in a workbook that stores formulas. OxFunc evaluates values, not stored formula text.
entries.expected_behavior: A1 stores =1+2, so FORMULATEXT(A1) returns the text "=1+2".

entries.why_context_sensitive: Table1[Amount] is a structured reference resolved against a workbook table definition (header row, body range, current region). Resolving the column to a range requires the table model.
The operand lives on a different sheet. Resolving Sheet2!A1:A3 requires a multi-sheet workbook model the local OxFunc resolver does not carry.
A1# is the spill-range reference anchored at A1. Its extent is determined by what the A1 dynamic-array formula spilled, which only exists after the workbook recalculates the anchor.
entries.expected_behavior: A1 spills {1;2;3}; A1# is A1:A3; SUM = 6.

entries.why_context_sensitive: BYROW binds an inline LAMBDA and invokes it per row. Forming and invoking the callable is formula-binding scope owned by the OxFml binder, not the OxFunc value surface in isolation.
entries.expected_behavior: Row sums spill as a 2x1 column {3;7}.

entries.why_context_sensitive: LET introduces named bindings into formula scope before evaluating the body. The name-binding step is OxFml formula-binding scope, not a pure function call.

VALUE parses text to a number through a LocaleFormatContext parser (value_fn.rs). OxFunc does not ship a local locale parser; the capability bundle is supplied through the typed seam (W082). Without it, VALUE("2") returns #VALUE! locally. This row was reclassified from a Category-2 probe to Category 1 on the first run of the evaluation-class lane (W104), demonstrating the classifier.
entries.expected_behavior: With a locale capability bundle supplied downstream, VALUE("2") returns the number 2.
